extracted.intended_audience: early-18th-century literate public; readers and aspiring writers/poets interested in imagination, moral essays, and literary taste
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and exemplars for imaginative writing: how to evoke the sublime (especially the sea/storm), use dreams as creative material, shape moral storytelling, and characterise married persons; also brief practical notes on publishing/format and the use of authoritative quotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describing the sublime (sea/storms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gather together those Circumstances which are the most apt to terrify the Imagination, and which really happen in the raging of a Tempest; a troubled Ocean gives the Imagination one of the highest kinds of Pleasure that can arise from Greatness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer large, real, and terrifying particulars over 'little Fancies.' Use circumstances that actually occur in storms to terrify and elevate the reader's imagination (as Longinus praises in Homer). The Psalm's depiction is offered as a model of nobility: present an overwhelming, unified image (tumult and recovery) rather than fragmented or fanciful details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use dreams as source of invention and demonstration of mind's activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Dreams are great instances of the activity natural to the human Soul, which sleep does not deaden; in dreams invention prompts readily and the mind often composes with ease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ dream-material for invention and imaginative episodes: dreams can supply fluent invention, heightened passions, vivid multiplicity of ideas, and devotional intensity. When writing dream-scenes, lean into the soul's agility, unexpected language facility, and intensified feelings to generate striking images or plot devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral justice in storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: The Mind of Man is naturally a Lover of Justice, and when we read a Story wherein a Criminal is overtaken... the Soul enjoys a certain Revenge for the Offence done to its Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft stories with a credible moral imprimatur or authoritative basis and, when appropriate to audience taste, provide the satisfaction of justice (villains exposed or punished). Prefer narratives 'for the truth of which there is good authority'—historical or well-attested anecdotes increase readers' moral pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterising married persons: virtues to depict
rubrics_metrics.description: Marriage is an Institution calculated for a constant Scene of as much Delight as our Being is capable of; two persons...have bound themselves to be good-humour'd, affable, discreet, forgiving, patient and joyful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When depicting marriage, emphasise mutual comfort, friendship, patience, discretion, forgiveness, and the ability of spouses to sustain both serious and joyous intercourse. Present friendship between spouses as a higher, enduring pleasure that should supplant transient passions; avoid reducing marriage to mere gratification of pleasure or fashions of dissolute behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support literary claims with authoritative quotations and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: The essay repeatedly invokes classical and sacred authorities (Longinus, Homer, the Psalmist, Plutarch, Tertullian) to illustrate and justify judgments about imagination, dreams, and the sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bolster aesthetic or moral claims by quoting respected sources and exemplary passages; use canonical examples (poetry, scripture, classical criticism) as models and evidence to persuade readers of taste or argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical considerations for publication and readership
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider price, format and portability for readers: print in little portable volumes, sell by volume for economy, and position issues as suitable presents for social occasions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing periodical or short-form literary works, attend to cost and physical format (portability, compact volumes) to broaden readership. Offering collected volumes and marketing them as appropriate gifts can increase circulation; be mindful of pricing in relation to readers' everyday expenditures.
